events.title: Abraham Lincoln Is Shot at Ford's Theatre
events.description: While attending a play at Ford's Theatre in Washington, D.C., President Abraham Lincoln was shot by actor John Wilkes Booth. He died the following morning.
events.significance: Lincoln was the first U.S. president to be assassinated. His death, days after the Civil War effectively ended, changed the course of Reconstruction.

events.title: RMS Titanic Strikes an Iceberg
events.description: Late on the night of April 14, the luxury liner RMS Titanic hit an iceberg in the North Atlantic off Newfoundland on her maiden voyage. She sank in the early hours of April 15.
events.significance: The sinking killed more than 1,500 people. It led to major reforms in maritime safety, including lifeboat requirements and round-the-clock radio watches.

events.title: Black Sunday Dust Storm Hits the Great Plains
events.description: A huge dust storm swept across the U.S. Midwest and Southern Plains. It darkened the skies and buried farms in drifting dirt during the Dust Bowl years.
events.significance: The event brought national attention to the Dust Bowl crisis. It helped spur federal soil conservation efforts.

events.title: Space Shuttle Columbia Returns from Its First Flight
events.description: Columbia, the first Space Shuttle, landed after its maiden orbital mission, which lasted about two days.
events.significance: It proved that a reusable, winged spacecraft could fly into orbit and return to land. That opened a new era of human spaceflight.
